ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the three vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all on the grid points of a square. What is the value of $\cos A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: Draw $BD\perp AC$ at D,\\
By the Pythagorean theorem,\\
$AB=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt{2}$, $AC=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}=\sqrt{10}$,\\
$\because$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}BC\times 3$, thus $CD=\frac{3\times 2}{3\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$,\\
In triangle $\triangle ABD$, $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, $AC=\sqrt{10}$, $CD=\sqrt{2}$,\\
$AD=\sqrt{AC^2-CD^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{10})^2-(\sqrt{2})^2}=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\cos A=\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{10}}=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: Draw $BD\perp AC$ at D,\\ By the Pythagorean theorem,\\ $AB=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt{2}$, $AC=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}=\sqrt{10}$,\\ $\because$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}BC\times 3$, thus $CD=\frac{3\times 2}{3\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$,\\ In triangle $\triangle ABD$, $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, $AC=\sqrt{10}$, $CD=\sqrt{2}$,\\ $AD=\sqrt{AC^2-CD^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{10})^2-(\sqrt{2})^2}=2\sqrt{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ $\cos A=\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{10}}=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC on grid paper, and B and C are located on the same horizontal grid line; counting the squares in the figure shows that C is 2 squares to the right of B, and A is 3 squares to the right of B and 3 squares above it, that is, A is 1 square to the right of C and 3 squares above it.
Then reason: Establish a coordinate system in grid units, taking B=(0,0), C=(2,0), A=(3,3). The requirement is cos A, that is, the cosine of the angle between vectors AB and AC. Starting from A, vector AB=B-A=(-3,-3), vector AC=C-A=(-1,-3). Use the dot product formula: AB·AC=(-3)(-1)+(-3)(-3)=3+9=12. |AB|=sqrt(3^2+3^2)=3sqrt2, |AC|=sqrt(1^2+3^2)=sqrt10. Therefore cos A=12/(3sqrt2·sqrt10)=12/(3sqrt20)=12/(6sqrt5)=2/sqrt5=2sqrt5/5.
